significant water penetration (a problem first noted in the 1950s). internal render is breaking down, and paintwork is peeling off the walls. humidity levels in the building are high and water saturation of walls is reducing thermal performance making the building difficult to heat and maintain. investigative repo rts were carried out to identify and remedy the sources of moisture penetration. these included a measurement survey and structural , stained glass, services, asbestos, and building condition reports. temporary screens were erected to test the performance of the wall structure. a specialist conservation contractor carried out drill testing o f the walls which confirmed significant water-logging of wall cores. a conservation management plan was commissioned to guide the remedial works and to aid in making applications for grant funding. in february 2026 an application was made to mayo county council for permission to carry out repair works to remedy wall damp initially on 2 bays of the west wall, replace the bell tower roof and resurface the gravel path connecting the two entrances. in november 2026 an application will be made to mayo county council prayer the former archbishop of tuam, joseph cunnane wasn’t too fond of driving and so during confirmation season he had the habit of getting one of the curates in tuam to drive him around the diocese. at one point however it happened that a certain curate wasn’t a particularly good driver – he had no sense of direction and seemed to have a total lack peripheral vision. when it was suggested to the archbishop that particular curate might be left off the rota the archbishop declined declaring that the curate in question was doing wonders for his (the archbishop’s) prayer life! i was on duty in clare island last weekend. there is now mass on the island on every second weekend and duty entails that a priest takes the ferry out from roonagh on the friday evening to say the 8pm mass on the island. he then stays over in the priest’s house and after saying an early morning mass leaves again for roonagh. it’s always a nice experience and the islanders will always have a fire down and some food left for the visiting priest. i was aware that the forecast for last weekend was iffy at best but by friday morning it was clear that the weather would play a factor in whether there would be mass on the island or not. as it happened there was a month’s mind mass scheduled for friday evening so with family home it wasn’t easy to cancel. before i left newport i confirmed that there was a boat from roonagh at 6pm but i hadn’t reached westport when the ferry company rang me to say that there would be only one boat off the island on saturday morning and that would be to cloughmore in achill. after a few quick phonecalls i had organised that i’d leave my car in westport, get the bus out to roonagh and that the priest in achill would bring me from cloughmore back up to newport on saturday morning. the sea was pretty choppy on the way out but by saturday morning it was a whole different affair. when i arrived down at the pier the swell was high as i spotted the boat appearing around the headland being pounded by the waves as it rose and then disappeared in the heavy seas. heading to cloughmore it was a case of holding on for dear life. i have a good sea stomach but still prefer to stay outside on deck meaning that with the rain and the spray there was no possibility of keeping dry. halfway across, with the boat being heavily buffeted by wind and sea visibility became so bad that we couldn’t see land in any direction. as i prayed earnestly to see mulranny just one more time the truth of archbishop cunnane’s declaration dawned on me. my prayers were answered when gradually land reappeared on the horizon and we arrived safe and wet in cloughmore. it is certainly very easy to pray when your life is in god’s hands! but aren’t our lives always thirtieth sunday in ordinary time to love the lord with all our heart – is this even possible?

a common assumption is that love must just come, that it grows organically, and that it cannot be forced . that’s infatuation, not true love . any kind of love – for a parent, spouse, child, or friend – will reach a point during which it is no longer easy.
for love to be true, it must be a free choice and commitment. ‘all your heart, soul, and mind’ sounds rather extreme, even rather dangerous.
the world says that loving anyone totally is a risky proposition – what if the one we love rejects us or lets us down, leaving us with nothing?
and the world is even more terrified to love god totally, who cannot even be seen.
this makes sense; after all, to love totally is to trust that we will find fulfilment precisely by not looking for it ourselves, but by looking to fulfil someone else.
that old, al most clichéd phrase, ‘love grows when it is given away ,’ is actually spot-on in this regard.

true love takes a leap of faith, which is what frightens nonbelievers . many people are okay with going to church every now and then or volunteering for a charity from time to t ime(and posting it on instagram, of course).
loving like that does not require us to make an y kind of leap, any kind of definitive change, any commitment.
but loving god with everything means that all do is for love of him.
we trust that he will take care of us. that is heroic; that is what it means to bea saint.
